prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1195; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by the third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Both vehicles drivable from scene, though insured reports neck and knee discomfort. Recorded statement scheduled with insured.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from insured. Insured describes stopping abruptly and feeling a jolt to the knee against the lower dash. Denies prior knee complaints in the last several years. Photos of insured vehicle rear bumper and interior received and saved to file.

Entry 3: Claimant is now represented by counsel. All further contact to be routed through the attorney's office. Letter of representation received and logged. Request for medical records and authorization forms sent to counsel. Diary set for follow-up in two weeks.

Entry 4: Medical records received from treating provider. Records document knee contusion with ongoing pain and limited range of motion. MRI ordered by treating physician, results pending. Reviewed records against the reported mechanism of injury; consistent with a low-to-moderate impact. Referred file to medical bill review for itemization.

Entry 5: Counsel's demand package received and reviewed. Demand includes medical specials, lost wages documentation, and a general damages claim tied to the knee injury. Liability accepted on the insured's side is not indicated, so the third-party carrier has been notified. Reserve reviewed and adjusted. Supervisor review requested before any response to counsel.
